<p class="specimen-kind">Theorem 2.12</p>
<p class="specimen-name">Strong Law of Large Numbers</p>

Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots$ be i.i.d. random variables with $\mathbb E|X_i| < \infty$. Let $\mathbb E X_i = \mu$ and $S_n = X_1 + \cdots + X_n$. Then

$$
\frac{S_n}{n} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{a.s.}} \mu \qquad \text{as } n \to \infty.
$$

:::

[A theorem as it appears in [Applied Probability](content/notes/advanced-applied-probability/2.qmd#thm-aap-2-13).]{.specimen-source}

:::
